 Air India Nears Completion of Cabin Upgrades on Heathrow Routes
 By Mark Caswell
 Published 19th October 2026 
 From January the carrier's Bengaluru-Heathrow service will be operated by a retrofitted 787-8 aircraft, and capacity is also being added on selected flights to Birmingham and Gatwick
 Credit: Image courtesy of Air India 
 Passengers travelling to and from London Heathrow with Air India will soon be guaranteed to experience the carrier’s latest cabins.
 The airline has been steadily rolling out new and retrofitted aircraft across its Heathrow services, and from January 2027 Air India’s flights between Bengaluru and the London hub will switch from a legacy Boeing 787-8 to an upgraded Dreamliner aircraft.
 The retrofitted Boeing jet features new economy and business class seating, and passengers will also benefit from the option of premium economy on the Bengaluru-Heathrow route.
 When Air India launched flights between Bengaluru and London in August 2024 they initially operated to/from Gatwick Airport , but the service quickly switched to Heathrow in October of the same year .
 The carrier’s flights between Delhi and London Heathrow already operate with a mix of new Airbus A350-900 and Boeing 787-9 aircraft, while its Mumbai-Heathrow route is served by either new 787-9s or retrofitted 787-8s.
 Credit: Image courtesy of Air India 
 Air India’s Transformation Continues
 Air India is in the midst of a comprehensive transformation programme under the Tata Group, with initiatives including new seating and uniforms , revamped lounges, a redesigned livery and record aircraft orders .
 The airline took delivery of its first A350-900 in late 2023 , configured with 28 suites in business class and 24 premium economy seats. Air India also welcomed the first of 20 new Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners into its fleet this summer , and has been busy retrofitting existing 777-300ER and 787-8 aircraft.
 Meanwhile on the ground the carrier unveiled its revamped lounge at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport earlier this year. It also opened a new space at San Francisco Airport featuring a speakeasy-style bar and private first class zone .
 But it hasn’t all been plain sailing – supply chain delays have led the airline to retrofit selected older aircraft rather than retire them as originally planned.
 And CEO Campbell Wilson resigned earlier this year , less than a year after a fatal crash killed a total of 260 people shortly after take-off from Ahmedabad. Last month Reuters reported Air India is seeking $1.5 billion in fresh equity from ‌its owners Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines, following record losses.
 Credit: Image courtesy of Air India 
 Advertisement 
 Advertisement 
 Capacity Increases to Birmingham and Gatwick
 Alongside the completion of cabin upgrades on Air India’s Heathrow routes, the carrier has also boosted capacity on selected UK services.
 The airline’s four-times-weekly Gatwick-Ahmedabad flights now offer 2,700 additional seats per month each way, following the replacement of the Boeing 787-8 that had been serving the route with a larger 777-300ER aircraft.
 Similarly, Air India’s thrice-weekly Amritsar-Birmingham flights are now being served with the 777-300ER, adding 2,000 extra seats per month each way to the route.
 However, Air India has confirmed that the 777-300ER aircraft now serving the two routes above do not currently feature the carrier’s latest seating products.
 In total the airline now operates a total of 57 weekly nonstop flights across seven UK routes, as follows:
 Ahmedabad – Gatwick
 Amritsar – Birmingham
 Amritsar – Gatwick
 Bengaluru – Heathrow
 Delhi – Birmingham
 Delhi – Heathrow
 Mumbai – Heathrow
 Out of Heathrow Air India competes with British Airways and Virgin Atlantic – both of which operate flights to Bengaluru, Delhi and Mumbai.
 Rival Indian carrier IndiGo also launched flights to Heathrow from Delhi and Mumbai last year, but these services are being suspended from 25 October as the airline battles geopolitical tensions, restricted airspace and elevated fuel prices.
 Credit: Image courtesy of Air India 
 The Bottom Line
 More than three years on from unveiling its new brand identity , Air India will finally be able to offer a consistent premium product offering on key flights to and from London Heathrow.
 Business Traveller reviewed the carrier’s A350-900 Collins Horizon business class product last year . The sense of privacy was impressive, as was the seat width and the storage options.
 Revamped inflight and ground services are helping to rebuild the airline’s reputation following the Indian government’s divestment of the carrier in 2022. But persistent losses suggest Air India has a way to go before it can be considered a credible global challenger.
 Meanwhile, former British Airways boss Willie Walsh is now CEO at rival IndiGo , as the airline looks to triple its fleet size and fulfil long-haul ambitions in the coming years.
